clue.text: Shabby? Study pub featured in article

indicators.note: something featured in a thing appears within it, so the study and pub words sit inside the article

parts.note: the definite article is the word 'the'
to read a subject is to study it at university
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A dingy reading room in a pub is described in a newspaper article.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes worn so thin that the weave shows are shabby; the question mark flags the figurative stretch.

clue.text: Kid not right for a moment

indicators.note: 'not right' tells us the letter for right is dropped from the trick word

parts.note: to kid someone is to trick them

explanation.surface: A child is told off for misbehaving at a particular instant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child, but it is the verb meaning to fool someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick is British slang for a very short time, as in 'back in a tick'.

clue.text: Complete game of golf with editor

parts.note: a round is one game of golf over the course

explanation.surface: A golfer finishes the course and has a newspaper editor along for the walk.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rounded or rounded off is whole and finished, so the adjective means complete.

clue.text: Soon enough exhausted, pleasure-seeking

parts.note: 'all in' is an idiom for utterly tired out
a 'good-time' person is one devoted to pleasure, as in good-time girl

explanation.surface: A party animal will tire out before long.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at the proper moment, eventually, without hurrying: a phrase for patience.

clue.text: Pinter play, a sell-out

definitions.meaning: Harold Pinter's 1978 drama tracing an affair backwards in time
a sell-out here is an act of disloyalty, giving someone up

explanation.surface: A theatre production by Harold Pinter plays to full houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sell-out' suggests a packed theatre, but here it means treachery.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling someone out is treachery, and Pinter named his play about adultery after that very deceit.

clue.text: Quarrelled as king due

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
money that is due is owed

explanation.surface: A monarch fell out with someone over money he was owed.
explanation.definitionFit: To row (rhymes with 'cow') is British for having a noisy argument.

clue.text: Go doolally when retired

indicators.note: retiring is withdrawing or going back, so the word for doolally is read backwards

parts.note: doolally is British slang for crazy, as is bats

explanation.surface: Someone loses their mind after giving up work.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a go and having a stab are both idioms for making an attempt.

clue.text: Two short tiers collapsed in tornado

indicators.note: short means lacking its final letter, so the number word is cut by one

parts.note: the number word spelt out

indicators.note: collapsed suggests the tiers falling into disorder, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tornado brought down a couple of stands that were not tall enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Twister is an American informal name for a tornado, from its spinning funnel.

clue.text: Through with sweeping, on the whole

parts.note: by can mean through, as in 'by means of'
and joins things, just as with does
sweeping changes are large ones

explanation.surface: Someone has finished cleaning and judges the result overall.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means generally or mostly, taking everything into account.

clue.text: Pair's masterstroke with lease

parts.note: a coup is a brilliant, successful move
to let a property is to lease it out

explanation.surface: Two people pull off a brilliant deal on a rental agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A couplet is two lines of verse that go together, usually rhyming.

clue.text: Working with CIA in Kansas city

indicators.note: working letters over means kneading them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An intelligence agent is cooperating with the CIA in a Midwest city.
explanation.definitionFit: Wichita is the largest city in the US state of Kansas.

clue.text: Taken by surprise, held out?

parts.note: caught means grasped and held
out can mean asleep or unconscious, as one napping is

explanation.surface: A question about someone ambushed and detained outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like 'outside' but means out cold, dozing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being found unprepared, like someone discovered asleep on duty.

clue.text: Note new Dundee stand completely finished

parts.note: do (or doh) is the first note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: new signals the letters being made anew in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A notice says the new grandstand in Dundee is entirely built.
explanation.walkthrough: Dundee is a Scottish city with two football grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means wholly over and dealt with, nothing left to do.

clue.text: Successful academic, one on board

parts.note: PROF is short for professor, an academic
I is the Roman numeral for one
a table is a board, as in 'bed and board'; something on the board is on the table

explanation.surface: A distinguished professor sits on a company's board.
explanation.definitionFit: A venture is successful in business terms when it makes money.

clue.text: One allotted a call sign, 'Aries', to receive Idaho broadcast

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so the zodiac animal takes the other letters inside

parts.note: Aries is the ram of the zodiac

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A sign of the zodiac picks up a transmission from Idaho.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aries' looks like a star sign in the surface, but only its animal matters; 'broadcast' fits the radio scene while signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateur radio operators are each issued an official call sign to identify their station.

clue.text: Guide that woman inside health resort

indicators.note: inside places the pronoun within the resort word

parts.note: a spa is a resort for taking health treatments
her is the pronoun for that woman

explanation.surface: A female guide works at a wellness retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are Himalayan people famed as mountain guides and porters on Everest expeditions.

clue.text: Supporter at home cross over display?

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for cross runs backwards

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix, as in rood screen
to post a notice is to display it

explanation.surface: A home fan is upset by what is shown on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter at home' suggests a home fan; read literally it is a structural support in a house.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright timber of a door frame holds the door up in a house.

clue.text: A daughter in appearance may give a deceptive impression

definitions.note: a phrase for a thing (the noun answer) that may give a false impression

indicators.note: in places the article and daughter inside the appearance word

parts.note: face can mean outward appearance, as in 'on the face of it'
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A girl's looks can mislead people.
explanation.definitionFit: A false front that hides the real nature of something; a building's frontage by origin.

clue.text: Return punch in bar

definitions.meaning: a blow struck back in reply, a counterpunch
a bar where drinks or goods are served across a flat top

explanation.surface: A boxer hits back in a pub fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A counter is both a retaliatory blow in boxing and the serving surface in a shop or pub.

clue.text: Follow party with good record

parts.note: to hound someone is to follow them relentlessly
a do is British informal for a party

explanation.surface: A fan trails a party that has a good track record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' looks like a track record but is a disc.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley's 1956 single of that name was a famous hit record.

clue.text: Party I'd assembled for outing

indicators.note: assembled means put together, so the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A group of people gather for an excursion.
explanation.definitionFit: An excursion there and back within a single day is an outing.

clue.text: IOM races trip, sort youth organised

definitions.note: IOM is the Isle of Man; the motorcycle road races held there

indicators.note: organised means arranged, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A trip to the Isle of Man races is arranged for young people.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea; its TT motorcycle races are world famous.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual motorcycle road racing festival on the Isle of Man goes by this name, TT for short.

clue.text: Dance tune's first on radio?

definitions.meaning: the first letter of tune is T, which radio operators say as a word in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A radio DJ opens the show with a dance number.
explanation.definitionFit: The ballroom dance shares its name with the NATO radio code word for the letter T.

clue.text: Stake in restaurant extended

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies within the run of letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A restaurant owner puts money into an expansion.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the ante is the stake each player puts in before the deal.

clue.text: Marsh bird pecked seabird

parts.note: pecked means bit, as a bird does
a tern is a slender seabird

explanation.surface: One bird attacks another with its beak.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a heron-like wading bird of reedbeds and marshland, famous for its booming call.

clue.text: Greek character's order, constant in golf club

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

indicators.note: in puts the constant inside the golf club word

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A Greek man is told to keep to rules at his golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour granted by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is the fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, short o.

clue.text: Win each service

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A tennis player takes every point on serve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests tennis but is an armed force.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn and to win can both mean to gain something through effort, such as respect.

clue.text: Something to eat in bed, e.g. pâté I spread

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: spread hints at the letters being spread about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone spreads pâté on a snack in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like spreading pâté on toast, but it is the anagram signal; the accents on pâté are ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: This British dish is minced beef under a mashed potato crust, so a thing to eat.
